attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stating his own hypothesis and how widely it is held.

semantics.note: The proposition says only that the view has spread, not that it is true. This matches the plain declarative statement. The 'since 2022' detail is kept as a qualifier.

contract.note: Marcus named no population or measure. The plain reading, visible broadening of skepticism about data-only scaling from 2022 to January 2025, is fair and ordinary. It counts endorsement, not majority agreement, and correctly warns that a slowdown is not the same as his full robustness thesis.

evidence.note: Independent Big Think profile dated before the post. It confirms Marcus's 2022 'Hitting a Wall' argument about reliability and reasoning limits, which verifies the advocacy timeline.

Attributed reproduction of a November 2024 Reuters report. Prominent scientists, including Sutskever, a former scaling advocate, were speaking out on the limits of bigger-is-better. This documents broadening within the period.
TIME, November 21, 2024, reports that the data-limits hypothesis has gained ground. Named researchers say scaling alone may be insufficient. Contemporaneous and independent.
Amodei, an industry figure speaking about his own field, stays confident in scaling. Continued disagreement limits any claim of consensus but does not contradict an increase in skepticism.

reviews.rationale: Independent reporting confirms Marcus argued in 2022 that deep learning faced limits on reliability and reasoning. Reuters and TIME (November 2024) document prominent figures, including Sutskever, publicly questioning whether pretraining scale alone is enough, and TIME says the hypothesis has gained ground. Amodei's opposing view shows disagreement, not a decline. Under the fair plain reading, increased prevalence by January 2025 is supported, though the sources do not show full agreement with Marcus's robustness thesis.
